name: Maya
role: Mother of Siddhartha and queen of the Shakyas, whose dream of a white elephant announced the birth of the Buddha.
fun_fact: Buddhist tradition says she died seven days after the birth and was reborn in the Tushita heaven, where the future Buddha later taught her.

name: Siddhartha Gautama
role: Prince of the Shakyas who left the palace, awakened under the bodhi tree and became the Buddha, the teacher honoured across Buddhist Asia.
fun_fact: His title Buddha means awakened one, and Tibetan tradition calls him Sangye, a name used across the schools rather than by one sect alone.

name: Mara
role: The Buddhist figure of temptation, fear and death, who attacks the meditating Siddhartha and is met with the earth-touching gesture.
fun_fact: Mara's name is related to a Sanskrit root meaning death, and many teachers read him as a personification of inner obstacles.

name: Milarepa
role: Eleventh-century Tibetan yogi and poet of the Kagyu lineage, known for his cave retreats, his songs and his devotion to his teacher Marpa.
fun_fact: He is said to have lived on nettles for so long that his body turned green, a detail Tibetan painters often recall.

name: Padmasambhava
role: Eighth-century Indian master honoured as Guru Rinpoche, credited by Tibetan tradition with taming local forces and helping to establish Samye.
fun_fact: Tibetan tradition says he concealed teachings as terma, treasure texts later found by revealers across the Himalayas.

name: Yeshe Tsogyal
role: Tibetan disciple and consort of Padmasambhava, remembered as a master in her own right and as the preserver of his teachings.
fun_fact: Tibetan tradition credits her with memorizing and hiding many of Padmasambhava's teachings, including the Padma bka' thang.

name: Kuntu Zangpo
role: The primordial buddha of Bon, whose name means All-Good and who represents the ground from which the highest Bon teachings arise.
fun_fact: Bon and the Nyingma school both honour a primordial buddha called Kuntu Zangpo or Samantabhadra, but their systems are not identical.

name: Drenpa Namkha
role: An eighth-century Bon master and scholar, remembered for preserving Bon teachings during a period of Buddhist royal patronage.
fun_fact: Bon tradition links him with the period of Padmasambhava and King Trisong Detsen, and later accounts make him a defender of Bon learning.

name: Tara
role: Bodhisattva of compassionate action and swift protection, widely invoked across Tibetan Buddhism and beloved as a female figure of refuge.
fun_fact: Tibetan tradition tells that Tara arose from the tears of Avalokiteshvara, and another story says she was a princess who chose rebirth as a woman to benefit beings.

name: Palden Lhamo
role: A fierce protector deity of Tibetan Buddhism, honoured as a guardian of the Dharma, of Tibet and of the Dalai Lama lineage.
fun_fact: Her chapels are often set apart and her images veiled, because her protective power is considered especially intense.
